params.name: LfsrType
comment: Lfsr width

params.name: LfsrDw
comment: Derived parameter, do not override

params.name: EntropyDw
comment: Width of output tap (from lfsr_q[StateOutDw-1:0])

params.name: StateOutDw
comment: Lfsr reset state, must be nonzero!

params.name: DefaultSeed
comment: Custom polynomial coeffs

params.name: CustomCoeffs
comment: If StatePermEn is set to 1, the custom permutation specified via StatePerm is applied to the
state output, in order to break linear shifting patterns of the LFSR. Note that this
permutation represents a way of customizing the LFSR via a random netlist constant. This is
different from the NonLinearOut feature below which just transforms the output non-linearly
with a fixed function. In most cases, designers should consider enabling StatePermEn as it
comes basically "for free" in terms of area and timing impact. NonLinearOut on the other hand
has area and timing implications and designers should consider whether the use of that feature
is justified.

params.name: StatePerm
comment: Enable this for DV, disable this for long LFSRs in FPV

params.name: MaxLenSVA
comment: Can be disabled in cases where seed and entropy
inputs are unused in order to not distort coverage
(the SVA will be unreachable in such cases)

params.name: ExtSeedSVA
comment: Introduce non-linearity to lfsr output. Note, unlike StatePermEn, this feature is not "for
free". Please double check that this feature is indeed required. Also note that this feature
is only available for LFSRs that have a power-of-two width greater or equal 16bit.

ports.name: seed_en_i
comment: load external seed into the state (takes precedence)

ports.name: seed_i
comment: external seed input

ports.name: lfsr_en_i
comment: enables the LFSR

ports.name: entropy_i
comment: additional entropy to be XOR'ed into the state

ports.name: state_o
comment: (partial) LFSR state output

localparams.name: LfsrIdxDw
comment: Width of the entropy input to be XOR'd into state (lfsr_q[EntropyDw-1:0])

functions.name: lrotcol
comment: left-rotates a matrix column by the shift amount

functions.name: revcol
comment: reverses a matrix column

functions.name: compute_next_state
comment: the code below is not meant to be synthesized,
but it is intended to be used in simulation and FPV
